newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dlr ends firmer as greenback demand eases.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dlr ends firmer as greenback demand eases.

text.p: The recently depreciating Taiwan dollar rebounded to a slightly higher close on Thursday due to easing demand for the greenback, dealers said.
The local dollar wavered in a narrow range throughout the session before finishing at T$27.942, compared with Wednesday's eight-year-low close of T$27.948.
"Demand for the U.S. dollar eased today after yesterday's heavy U.S. currency buying. Many people simply decide to take a break," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Turnover through dealers was US$280 million, down from Wednesday's brisk US$319.5 million.

Dealers expected the Taiwan dollar to continue to test its downside due to a combination of the American currency's persistent overseas strength and foreign equity fund outflows triggered by recent profit-taking in Taiwan's stock market.
On Thursday, the local bourse recovered from a two-day profit-taking binge to close at 9,632.42, a gain of 251.36 points or 2.68 percent compared to Wednesday's 9,381.06 close.
Dealers said offshore speculation in the form of non-delivery forward trading, as was seen in early July during southeast Asia's currency crisis, was not obvious in Thursday's session.
"Speculators are always the market's key participants, but I think they've started to find out that Taiwan is very different from other Southeast Asian countries," the dealer said.
"Taiwan is not a market where speculators can manipulate things easily," the dealer said.

Central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong last week gave his most explicit comment to date on the speculative pressures that have undermined several southeast Asian currencies in July -- saying Taiwan's dollar was not vulnerable.
A T$27.92-97 range was seen for Friday.
